item.title: Stop Polling for Releases, Let Them Push to Your CI: Angelia, a Self-Hosted Release Event Bus
item.description: GitHub Actions cannot react to a release of someone else’s repository, so plugin maintainers poll on a cron that GitHub says can be late or dropped. Angelia watches PyPI, npm, crates.io, GitHub and GitLab for you and pushes one signed event per new version. Home Assistant 2026.11.2 was detected 3 seconds after it was published and tested in my integration’s CI an hour later. And 10,000 watches fit in 1 vCPU and 256 MB.

item.title: Home Assistant Ships Every Month: a CI That Reads the Release Notes, Opens an Issue and Waits for a Label
item.description: A bug report led me to a nightly check that had been green for weeks while twelve tests failed. The new CI has three layers. Deterministic checks that really fail, a Claude review of each Home Assistant monthly release posted as an issue (about $1.17 a run), and a label that asks Claude to open a fix PR with six narrow tools. The diagrams, the security model, the first real review, and a narrated video.
